989:
The chairperson of the Meriwether County Commission shall open the hearing with an explanation of the purpose of the hearing and a description of the general rules for the conducting of the hearing, The chairperson or his delegate may describe the authority and role of the commission in any zoning decision. The chairperson or his delegate shall chair the hearing and shall determine the relevance of any proposed comment or presentation to the commission in the hearing and is authorized to rule any individual or a portion of any presentation out of order if not relevant to the published purpose of the hearing. Any person addressing the chairperson and commission shall respond to questions of the chairperson and commission. Remarks shall be made to the chairperson only and not to other members of the commission or audience. Any portion of allotted time unused by either the applicant or opponent shall not invalidate any proceedings or action taken on the proposed amendment. The following rules of procedure govern the public hearing on rezoning or similar matters (special uses) before the Meriwether County Commission. These rules apply to all such public hearing items appearing on any agenda:
(1) Procedures relating to application, notice, and advertisement of items on the public hearing agenda shall conform to the requirements of Georgia law and the Meriwether County codes.
(2) Exercise of the zoning power shall conform to the standards expressed in the Meriwether County Zoning Ordinance, as most recently amended, as well as with the comprehensive land use plan.
(3) The zoning administrator shall provide copies of the policies required by O.C.G.A. § 36-66-1 et seq., which copies shall be available on request to interested members of the public.
(4) Individuals desiring to address the county commission regarding an agenda item are required to contact the county clerk. Applicants and/or proponents of an item on the public hearing agenda shall be heard first and shall have a minimum of ten minutes and no more than 20 minutes in which to present any information pertinent to the issue to be decided. Failure of the applicant or his representative to be present for the hearing shall result in automatic termination of any proceedings on the amendment and a negative recommendation on the proposed amendment by the chairperson and commission of Meriwether County. Opponents of the issue may respond and shall have a minimum of ten minutes and a maximum of 20 minutes in which to present any information pertinent to the issue to be decided. Applicants or opponents will each be given an additional five minutes for rebuttal. Either the applicant or opponent, however, shall not discuss new issues during the rebuttal.
(5) In the event there is more than one speaker per side, speakers must divide their time or designate a spokesperson in order to complete their full presentation within the time allotment. Each side shall have equal time overall.
(6) The time allotments described above may be modified by a majority vote of the commissioners present at said meeting based on the request of the applicant and/or opponent.
(7) Any remark amounting to an attack on the character or personal integrity of another individual, comment not factually supportable, comment in the form of an emotional outburst, or comment not directed at the chairperson, shall be considered to be non-relevant to the purpose of the hearing and shall be ruled out of order.
(8) The chairperson or his delegate shall enter into the record after the presentation of the applicant or his representative any written comment, petition, or similar written statement received by the county prior to the hearing and the same shall be considered by the chairperson and commission along with comments and other relevant information of the hearing in making any zoning decision concerning the proposed zoning amendment. At the public hearing, the county commission shall review the reports prepared by the zoning administrator and planning commission.
(9) When proponents and opponents of the proposed zoning amendment have been heard in accordance with the foregoing procedures, the chairperson or his delegate shall declare the public hearing closed. No further public hearing on the proposed zoning amendment shall be required prior to the zoning decision.
(10) Copies of these procedures shall be provided at each public hearing.
(Ord. No. 2020-04, § 1(Exh. A), 8-25-2020)
990:
The county commission shall not consider any application until a minimum of five days has passed from the date of the public meeting before the planning commission that is set forth in section 16.6 of this ordinance. Furthermore, the county commission shall consider the standards in section 16.8 of this ordinance in evaluating each application. So that the purpose of this ordinance will be served, and the health, public safety, and general welfare secured, the county commission may approve the application, reduce the land area for which the application is made, change the district requested, add or delete conditions of the application, deny an application, or defer consideration of an application to acquire additional information. An action by the commission to defer the application shall include a statement of the date and time of the next meeting at which the application will be considered, which statement shall constitute public notice of the hearing on the application and no further notice is required.
(1) After the presentation of positions by members of the public at the public hearing, and at the regularly scheduled meeting of the county commission, a recommendation will be made from the Meriwether County staff (zoning administrator, planning commission).
(2) Following the staff recommendation, county commission members may ask if anyone present has questions pertinent to the issue.
(3) Following questions and/or comments by county commission members, a motion for action on the issue will be in order. A majority of affirmative votes of a quorum is required to pass any motion before the county commission.
(4) So that the purpose of the ordinance will be served, and health, public safety and general welfare secured, the commissioners are authorized the following action with respect to any motion pending before it consisting of one of the following: approval, approval with conditions, approval of a different zoning district than requested, denial, withdrawal, or deferral to a time and date specified in the minutes of the meeting. No official action shall be taken until there is a majority vote of the Meriwether County Commission.
(Ord. No. 2020-04, § 1(Exh. A), 8-25-2020)
991:
Purpose. These regulations establish a board of appeals and provide a mechanism for relief in an individual case where the applicant requests relief from a decision by the planning commission on variances due to hardship or from actions of the zoning administrator in the administration or enforcement of this Code. The grant of authority and powers delegated by the Meriwether County commissioners is limited to the provisions set forth in this ordinance. Any appeals of the decision of the board of zoning appeals shall be directed to the appropriate court of Meriwether County.
(Ord. No. 2020-04, § 1(Exh. A), 8-25-2020)
992:
A board of appeals is hereby established. Said board shall consist of three voting members, who are residents and registered voters of the county, each of who shall serve for terms of three years beginning January 5, through January 5 of each year. None of the members of the board of appeals shall be a member of the county commission or planning commission. The board of commissioners shall appoint the board members. Members are removable for cause by the county commission, failure to attend three consecutive meetings or any four meetings in a calendar year shall be considered automatic resignation from the board of appeals, and upon such resignation or other vacancies in office, the chairperson or the zoning administrator shall inform the county commission of such occurrence as promptly as possible, so that the commission may appoint a replacement to fill the unexpired term.
(Ord. No. 2020-04, § 1(Exh. A), 8-25-2020)
993:
The board of appeals shall adopt rules of procedure as are necessary to carry out the purposes of its authority. Meetings shall be held only on an as-needed basis and shall be open to the public. The board shall appoint a secretary, who shall be the zoning administrator, unless otherwise designated, to record the minutes of its proceedings, showing the action of each board member upon each question. The board shall keep records of its examinations and other official actions, all of which shall be filed with the zoning administrator and be public records. The zoning administrator shall serve as the advisor to the board, except in cases of an appeal from a decision of the community development department. The board may adjourn any public hearing or meeting in order to obtain additional information, or to serve further notice upon such other property owners as it decides may be interested in the application or appeal; provided however, that the board shall act on all applications within 60 days of the date the initial meeting on the matter was held.
(Ord. No. 2020-04, § 1(Exh. A), 8-25-2020)
994:
Any person who alleges there is an error in, or who is aggrieved by, a decision of the zoning administrator in the administration, enforcement, and/or interpretation of this Code may file an appeal through the community development office to the county administration within 30 days of the decision, stating the grounds for such appeal. Decisions on variance made by the planning commission may be appealed to the board of appeals, The board of appeals is hereby authorized to hear and decide said appeals, after proper application, public meeting and adoption of relevant findings of fact.
An appeal from a ruling of the zoning administrator or an appeal from a variance decision by the planning commission shall stop all proceedings in furtherance of the action being appealed. The board may affirm, overrule or modify, in whole or in part, the rulings of the zoning administrator or planning commission variance ruling. In cases where an appeal is granted, the board shall have all necessary powers to direct the issuance of building permits and land use permits not otherwise inconsistent with this Code and any other code, resolution, or ordinance adopted by the county commission,
(Ord. No. 2020-04, § 1(Exh. A), 8-25-2020)
995:
Upon the filing of a complete application for an appeal with the zoning administrator, a due process hearing shall be scheduled and held on the proposed appeal. Notice of the hearing shall be given and the hearing shall be conducted as provided for in the previous section of this Code.
(Ord. No. 2020-04, § 1(Exh. A), 8-25-2020)
996:
No building or other structure shall be located, erected, moved, added to, or structurally altered without a building permit issued by the zoning administrator, No building permit shall be issued except in conformity with the provisions of this ordinance.
(Ord. No. 2020-04, § 1(Exh. A), 8-25-2020)
997:
All applications for building permits shall be accompanied by a set of plans, drawn to scale, a copy of the deed and plat showing the actual dimensions of the lot to be built upon, the sizes and locations on the lot of any existing buildings or structures, the shape, size, height, use and location on the lot of the building or structure proposed to be erected or altered, setback distances, any parking spaces, and such other information as may be necessary to provide for the enforcement of the provisions of this ordinance. If no substantial construction progress has been made within six months of the date of the issuance of the building permit, the permit becomes invalid.
(Ord. No. 2020-04, § 1(Exh. A), 8-25-2020)
998:
(a) A certificate of occupancy issued by the zoning administrator is required in advance of the use or occupancy of:
(1) Any lot or a change in the use of the lot.
(2) A building hereafter erected or altered or a change in the use of an existing building.
(3) Any nonconforming use that exists at the time of the enactment of this ordinance or an amendment thereto that is changed, extended, altered, or rebuilt thereafter.
(b) The certificate of occupancy shall state specifically wherein the nonconforming use fails to meet the provisions of this ordinance.
(c) No certificate of occupancy shall be issued, unless the lot or building or structure complies with all provisions of this ordinance.
(d) A record of all certificates of occupancy shall be kept on file in the office of the zoning administrator and a copy shall be furnished on request to any person having a proprietary or tenancy interest in the building or land involved.
(Ord. No. 2020-04, § 1(Exh. A), 8-25-2020)
999:
(a) In order to maintain the health, safety, welfare, and morality of the citizens of Meriwether County, the county commissioners may impose conditions on rezoning requests. Conditions placed on the property as a part of approval of a rezoning application shall remain in force until such time as an appeal has been granted. Conditions shall be in writing and the purpose for the conditions shall be established.
(b) Conditions placed on property at the time of rezoning shall become a written part of the minutes of the county commission meeting and shall be attached to the amendment to the official zoning map. The conditions imposed shall be part of the rezoning application and kept in the office of the zoning administrator. Conditions on the property travel with the property and stay in effect when property changes owners.
(Ord. No. 2020-04, § 1(Exh. A), 8-25-2020)
1000:
Appeals for relief of conditions placed on rezoned property may be heard by the Meriwether County Commission only when the reason for the placement of conditions has been altered to allow the use of the property without the conditions. Appeals shall follow the same procedure as that of a rezoning application. Public hearings are required.
(Ord. No. 2020-04, § 1(Exh. A), 8-25-2020)
1001:
(a) The planning commission shall review and the Meriwether County Commission shall approve or deny special uses that are specifically authorized by this ordinance. Public hearings are required. (See hearing requirements.)
(b) Conditions and limitations. The planning commission shall include any condition, requirement, or limitation that may be necessary to protect adjacent properties and carry out the provisions of this ordinance in its review and the Meriwether County Commission may impose conditions, requirements or limitations it deems necessary. If at any time after a special use permit has been issued, the zoning administrator finds that the conditions imposed and the agreements made have not been or are not being fulfilled by the holder of a special use permit, the permit shall be terminated.
(c) Procedure. Application for a special use shall be filed with the office of the zoning administrator, and the planning commission shall have 45 days within which to consider each request and make written recommendations to the county commission. A public hearing is required by the county commission (see public hearing requirements). Upon receiving recommendations from the planning commission or after the 45-day period has expired, the county commission shall schedule the proposed special use to be voted on at the next regularly scheduled commission meeting. Each application shall contain a simple sketch of the site, showing the following:
(1) The general location of all existing structures and property lines.
(2) Present zoning of adjacent property.
(3) The existing use of adjacent property.
(4) Location of proposed buildings and land use.
(5) A legal description of the property.
(6) Setbacks.
(7) Parking spaces, if applicable.
(d) Specifically, in order to grant approval of a special use, the county commission must find the following standards have been met:
(1) The available existing street system is adequate to efficiently and safely accommodate the traffic that will be generated by the proposed use or development.
(2) The existing public utilities, facilities and services are adequate to accommodate the proposed use or development.
(3) The use or development will not generate or cause conditions such as noise, light, glare, and an odor, or similar objectionable features which would reduce the value, use or enjoyment of surrounding properties.
(4) The use would not have a detrimental environmental impact on the surrounding area.
(5) The use would not adversely affect the health, safety, morals, and general welfare of the community.
(6) Each application for a special use shall be assessed a fee according to the fee schedule posted in the community development office, set by the Meriwether County Commission, to partially defray administrative and notification costs.
(Ord. No. 2020-04, § 1(Exh. A), 8-25-2020)
1002:
(a) Any person, firm, or corporation violating a provision of this ordinance shall be guilty of a misdemeanor, and upon conviction, shall be punished by the imposition of a fine not to exceed $1,000.00, by imprisonment in the county jail for a period of time not to exceed 60 days, or by both such fine and imprisonment, or up to the limits of any authorized penalty provided by general law. Each day any violation of this Code or other ordinance shall continue shall constitute a separate offense.
(b) In the event any building is erected, constructed, reconstructed, altered, repaired, converted, or maintained, or any building, lot or acreage is used in violation of this ordinance, the county commission, zoning administrator, or any other appropriate authority, or any person who would be damaged by such violation, in addition to other remedies, may institute injunction, mandamus, or other appropriate action in proceeding to prevent said violation in the case of each such building or use.
(Ord. No. 2020-04, § 1(Exh. A), 8-25-2020)
1003:
This article of the Meriwether County Zoning Ordinance, as from time to time amended, is intended to set forth and constitute the policies, procedures and standards required under O.C.G.A. § 36-66-5, and copies of same shall be available to the public upon request.
(Ord. No. 2020-04, § 1(Exh. A), 8-25-2020)
1005:
This ordinance is not intended to interfere with or annul any easement, covenant, or other agreement between parties. However, where this ordinance imposes a greater restriction upon the use of property or by private easements, covenants, or agreements, the provisions of this ordinance shall govern. Whenever other ordinances or parts of ordinances require greater restrictions than those required by this ordinance, such ordinances or parts of ordinances shall govern.
(Ord. No. 2020-04, § 1(Exh. A), 8-25-2020)
1006:
All ordinances and parts of ordinances, regulations, or laws passed by the county commission of Meriwether County, Georgia, in conflict herewith, are hereby repealed. All ordinances or parts of ordinances not specifically in conflict herewith are hereby continued in force and effect.
(Ord. No. 2020-04, § 1(Exh. A), 8-25-2020)
1007:
Should any part, section, or provision of this ordinance be declared invalid or unconstitutional by any court of competent jurisdiction, such declared invalid or unconstitutional part, section or provision shall be deemed severed from this ordinance and shall not affect the validity of any remaining portion of this ordinance.
(Ord. No. 2020-04, § 1(Exh. A), 8-25-2020)
1008:
Footnote 1:

1010:
The purpose of this ordinance [appendix B] is to promote the health, safety, morals, convenience, order, prosperity, and general welfare of the municipality; to encourage economically sound and stable land development; to ensure the provisions of required streets, utilities, and other facilities and services to land development; to ensure the adequate provisions of safe and convenient traffic access and circulation, both vehicular and pedestrian, in land development; to ensure the provisions of needed public open spaces and public building sites in land development through the dedication or reservation of land for recreational, educational, and other public purposes; and to ensure that land developed in conformity with the Comprehensive Plan of Meriwether County, the county commissioners of Meriwether County, Georgia, do ordain and enact into law the following articles and sections. The subdivision regulations adopted by Resolution on October 14, 1991, as amended, is hereby repealed and replaced in its entirety by this subdivision ordinance which will be set out as appendix B to the Code of Ordinances, Meriwether County, Georgia.
(Ord. No. 2020-03, § 1(Exh. A), 8-25-2020)
1012:
This ordinance [appendix B] shall be known and may be cited as the Subdivision Regulations of Meriwether County, Georgia.
(Ord. No. 2020-03, § 1(Exh. A), 8-25-2020)
1014:
When used in these regulations, the following words and phrases shall have the meanings given in this section. Terms not herein defined shall have their customary dictionary meanings where not inconsistent with the context of these regulations. The term "shall" is mandatory. When not inconsistent with the context, words used in the singular number include the plural, and those used in the plural number include the singular. Words used in the present tense include the future. The term "person" includes a "firm," "association," "organization," "company" or "corporation," as well as an individual. The term "building" includes the term "structure."
Comprehensive plan means any part or element or the overall plan for development adopted by Meriwether County as provided by the General Planning Enabling Act of 1957, No. 358, as amended.
County means Meriwether County, Georgia.
Drainage plan means any plan or element thereof which has been approved by the director of community development.
Easement means a grant by the property owner of use, by the public, a corporation, or person(s), of a strip of land for a specific reason.
Final plat means a plat of a tract of land which meets the requirements of these regulations and is in a form for recording in the office of the clerk of the superior court.
Lot means a portion or parcel of land separated from the other portions or parcels by description as on a subdivision plat or record of survey map or as described by metes and bounds, and intended for transfer of ownership or for building development. For purposes of this ordinance [appendix], the term "lot" does not include any portion of a dedicated right-of-way.
Major street plan means the major street plan as adopted by Meriwether County as an element of the county comprehensive plan.
Planning commission means the Meriwether County Planning Commission.
Preliminary plat means a tentative plan of a proposed subdivision submitted to the community development department for its consideration.
Sanitarian means the Meriwether County Health Department.
Street means a way for vehicular traffic, whether or not designated as such on the Major Thoroughfare Plan of Meriwether County, to travel through and within the county.
(1) Major or arterial street means those streets designated as such on the Major Thoroughfare Plan of Meriwether County which serve as major traffic ways for travel through and within the county.
(2) Secondary or collector street means a street used to carry traffic from the "minor streets" to the "major streets" and includes, but is not limited to, the principal entrance and circulation streets of a subdivision.
(3) Minor or local street means a street used primarily for access to the abutting properties.
(4) Alley means a minor way used for service access to the back or side of properties otherwise abutting on a street.
(5) Cul-de-sac means a "minor street" having one end open to traffic and the other end permanently terminated with a paved turn-around.
(6) Dead end means a stub street in a subdivision which could at a later time be continued into another portion of the subdivision.
Subdivider means the person, firm, corporation, syndicate or other legal entity having such a proprietary interest in the land to be subdivided as will authorize the maintenance of proceeding to subdivide such land under this regulation, or the authorized agent of such person, firm or corporation for the purpose of undertaking activities covered by these regulations.
Subdivision means all divisions of a tract or parcel of land into more than three lots, excluding parent parcel, for the purpose, whether immediate or future, of sale or building development.
(Ord. No. 2020-03, § 1(Exh. A), 8-25-2020)
1016:
From and after the passage of this regulation, the community development department shall be the official authority, and no plat of land shall be entitled to record in the office of the clerk of superior court of Meriwether County, Georgia, unless it shall have the approval of the community development department inscribed thereon. The filing or recording of a final plat or a plat, minor final, without approval as required by this ordinance [appendix] is declared to be a misdemeanor.
(Ord. No. 2020-03, § 1(Exh. A), 8-25-2020; Ord. No. 2023-03, 10-24-2023)
1017:
The transfer of, sale of, agreement to sell, or negotiation to sell land by reference to or exhibition of, or other use of a plat of a subdivision that has not been given final approval as required by this ordinance [appendix] and recorded in the office of the clerk of the superior court of Meriwether County, Georgia, is prohibited, and the description by metes and bounds in the instrument of transfer or other document shall not exempt the transaction from penalties.
(Ord. No. 2020-03, § 1(Exh. A), 8-25-2020)
1018:
After this ordinance [appendix] shall have been put into effect, any subdivision that fails to meet the requirements of this ordinance [appendix] shall be disapproved by Meriwether County.
(Ord. No. 2020-03, § 1(Exh. A), 8-25-2020)
1019:
No public authority shall accept, improve or maintain any street not shown on an approved and recorded final plat unless such street shall have received the legal status of a public street prior to the adoption of the subdivision regulations set forth in the resolution of October 14, 1991.
(Ord. No. 2020-03, § 1(Exh. A), 8-25-2020)
1021:
All applications for plat approval for subdivisions shall be made to the community development department and accompanied by a fee determined from time to time by action of the board of commissioners. The applicable fee shall be set out in the county's consolidated fee schedule and made available for inspection during normal working hours in the community development office.
(Ord. No. 2020-03, § 1(Exh. A), 8-25-2020)
1022:
Following the pre-application review of a proposed subdivision and the payment of fees, the subdivider shall submit to the community development department the following:
(1) A letter requesting review and approval of a preliminary plat, giving the name and address of a person to whom the preliminary plat shall be sent.
(2) Five copies of the preliminary plat and any other related documents to be utilized as follows:
a. Community development department.
b. Public works department.
c. Health department.
d. County commissioners.
The fifth copy shall be returned to the subdivider or his agent with a notation of the action taken by Meriwether County.
(Ord. No. 2020-03, § 1(Exh. A), 8-25-2020)
1023:
(a) The community development department shall check the plat for conformance to this ordinance [appendix] and shall give notification by mail to the person designated in the letter requesting preliminary plat review and approval.
(b) Thereafter, the community development department shall give tentative approval or disapproval to the preliminary plat, including a statement of the reasons for disapproval if the preliminary plat is disapproved. One copy shall be returned to the subdivider or his agent and one copy added to the records of the community development department.
(c) Approval of a preliminary plat does not constitute approval of a final plat. It indicates only approval of the layout as a guide to the preparation of the final plat. Preliminary plat approval shall expire and be null and void after a period of one year, unless an extension of time is requested by the subdivider or his representative and is approved by the community development department.
(d) If action on a preliminary plat is not taken by the community development department within 45 days of the date of receipt (excluding weekends and holidays), the preliminary plat shall be considered approved, and a certificate of approval shall be issued on demand. However, the applicant for approval may waive this requirement and consent to an extension of time.
(Ord. No. 2020-03, § 1(Exh. A), 8-25-2020)
1025:
The preliminary plat shall be clearly and legibly drawn at a scale not smaller than 100 feet to one inch.
(Ord. No. 2020-03, § 1(Exh. A), 8-25-2020)
1026:
The preliminary plat shall show ground elevations, based on the datum plane of the U.S. Coast and Geodetic Survey (or other approved datum plane) with contour lines at intervals of not more than 20 feet for land that slopes more than five percent or contour lines at intervals of not more than five feet for land that slopes less than five percent.
(Ord. No. 2020-03, § 1(Exh. A), 8-25-2020)
1027:
The preliminary plat shall contain the following information:
(1) Name and address of the owner of record and of the subdivider.
(2) Proposed name of the subdivision and its acreage.
(3) North point and graphic scale and date.
(4) Vicinity map showing the location and acreage of the subdivision.
(5) Exact boundary lines of the tract of bearing and distance.
(6) Names of owners of record of adjoining property.
(7) Existing streets, utilities, and easements on and adjoining the tract.
(8) Proposed layout, including streets and alleys, to be reviewed by the community development department, with proposed street names, lot lines with dimensions, easements, land to be reserved or dedicated for public uses, and any land to be used for purposes other than single-family dwellings.
(9) Block numbers and lot numbers.
(10) Provisions for water supply, sewage and drainage, to be reviewed by the county sanitarian. Consult Meriwether County Health Department prior to submitting the application.
(11) Minimum building front yard setback lines as required by the county zoning ordinance.
(12) Soil types of the subdivision area from the U.S. Conservation Department Soil Study.
(Ord. No. 2020-03, § 1(Exh. A), 8-25-2020)
1028:
A certificate of approval of a preliminary plat by the community development department shall be inscribed on the plat as follows:
Pursuant to the land subdivision regulations of Meriwether County, Georgia, all the requirements of preliminary approval having been fulfilled, this preliminary plat was given preliminary approval by the director of community development on ________, 20___.
This preliminary plat approval does not constitute approval of a final plat. This certificate of preliminary plat approval shall expire and be null and void on ________ (one (1) year from preliminary plat approval).
County Community Development Official
Date
(Ord. No. 2020-03, § 1(Exh. A), 8-25-2020)
1030:
After the preliminary plat of the proposed land subdivision has been given tentative approval by the community development department, the subdivider may, within one year from tentative approval, submit to the Meriwether County Community Development Department:
(1) A letter requesting review and approval of a final plat and giving the name and address of the person to whom the final plat shall be sent.
(2) Five copies of the final plat and other related documents, as specified in article VI of this appendix.
(Ord. No. 2020-03, § 1(Exh. A), 8-25-2020)
1031:
(a) The community development department shall check the final plat for conformance with the tentatively approved preliminary plat, and with the rules and regulations, and shall notify by mail the person designated in the letter requesting final plat review and approval.
(b) Thereafter, the community development department shall approve or disapprove the final plat. A notation of the action shall be made on the original tracing and all prints of the final plat, including a statement of the reasons therefor if the final plat is disapproved.
(Ord. No. 2020-03, § 1(Exh. A), 8-25-2020)
1032:
Upon approval of the final plat, it shall be recorded in the office of the clerk of superior court of Meriwether County, Georgia. (The subdivider shall be responsible for recording of such final plat in the office of the clerk of superior court, Meriwether County, Georgia.)
(Ord. No. 2020-03, § 1(Exh. A), 8-25-2020)
1034:
The final plat shall conform to and meet the specifications of the preliminary plat, with the following additions:
(1) The final plat shall be clearly and legibly drawn and submitted per the requirements maintained in the office of the clerk of the superior court of Meriwether County. The final plat shall show:
a. Bearing and distances to the nearest existing street lines or benchmarks or other permanent monuments (one required) shall be accurately described on the plat.
b. County and land lot lines accurately tied to the lines of the subdivision by distances and angles when such lines traverse or are reasonably close to the subdivision.
c. Exact boundary lines of the tract, determined by a field survey.
d. Name of the subdivision, and the exact locations, widths, and names of all streets and alleys within and immediately adjoining the plat.
e. Street angles of deflection, angles of intersection, radii, and lengths of tangents.
f. Lot lines with dimensions to the nearest one-tenth-foot and bearing to the nearest minute.
g. Lots numbered in numerical order and blocks lettered alphabetically.
h. Locations, dimensions and purposes of easements and any areas to be reserved or dedicated for public use.
i. Accurate locations, materials and descriptions of monuments and markers.
j. A statement, either directly on the plat or in an identified attached document, of any private covenants.
k. A certification of a registered land surveyor stating that the land is not in a flood zone or floodway and does not lie in a basin below a Category II dam, as defined by Georgia Safe Dams Act.
l. Soil erosion control permit request for all areas within the subdivision, including roads and streets where the entire project is over one and one-tenth acres.

1036:
Land subject to flooding, improper drainage, or erosion or that is topographically or for other reasons unsuitable for residential use shall not be platted for residential use nor any other use that will continue or increase the danger to health, safety, or property destruction, unless the hazards can be and are corrected prior to final plat approval. No land shall be platted for use which would be in conflict with the floodplain or other zoning provisions in the county zoning ordinance and the state flood zone requirements. There shall be no construction other than sewer lines or utilities in areas construed as wetlands.
(Ord. No. 2020-03, § 1(Exh. A), 8-25-2020)
1037:
The name of the subdivision must have the approval of the Meriwether County Community Development Department, with verification from E-911. The name shall not duplicate or closely approximate the name of an existing subdivision. Any new subdivision development more than 50 lots must provide a secondary means of ingress and egress to the development via a street accepted into the county road system.
(Ord. No. 2020-03, § 1(Exh. A), 8-25-2020)
1038:
Subdivisions shall be located so as to gain access over a public street. Any new subdivision development with more than 50 lots must provide a secondary means of ingress and egress to the development via a street or road meeting Meriwether County requirements and specifications, and accepted into the Meriwether County Road System.
(Ord. No. 2020-03, § 1(Exh. A), 8-25-2020)
1039:
(a) All streets, thoroughfares, and other features of the Major Thoroughfare Plan of Meriwether County, Georgia, shall be taken into consideration by the subdivider.
(b) When features of other plans adopted by Meriwether County (such as school or other public building sites, parks, or other land for public uses) are located in whole or in part in a land subdivision, such features shall be either dedicated or reserved by the subdivider for acquisition within a reasonable time by the appropriate public agency.
(c) All access points into a subdivision that require the construction and acceptance of a new county road or street may be required to provide deceleration and/or acceleration lanes constructed to Meriwether County specifications. This requirement will be based on street or road classification, traffic volumes, and size of the development at the determination of Meriwether County.
(Ord. No. 2020-03, § 1(Exh. A), 8-25-2020)
1040:
The requirement of these regulations may be modified in the case of a large-scale community or neighborhood unit, such as a housing project or shopping center which is not subdivided into customary lots, blocks, and streets, if the development is approved by Meriwether County and if it is in conformity with the purpose and intent of these regulations.
(Ord. No. 2020-03, § 1(Exh. A), 8-25-2020)
1042:
Existing streets adjacent to a subdivision may be continued contingent upon prior approval by Meriwether County and shall meet road specification as required per this ordinance [appendix].
(Ord. No. 2020-03, § 1(Exh. A), 8-25-2020)
1043:
Street names require the approval of the community development department, after verification from E-911. Streets that are obviously in alignment with streets already existing and named shall be given the name of the existing street. Names of new streets shall not duplicate nor closely approximate those of existing streets.
(Ord. No. 2020-03, § 1(Exh. A), 8-25-2020)
1044:
Street jogs with centerline offsets of less than 125 feet shall not be permitted.
(Ord. No. 2020-03, § 1(Exh. A), 8-25-2020)
1045:
A cul-de-sac shall be provided at the closed end with a turn-around having a property line radius of at least 65 feet, and an outside pavement radius of at least 50 feet on non-curb and gutter sections, and 50 feet to back of curb on curb and gutter streets. Temporary turnarounds shall be provided for dead end streets which are scheduled to be extended at a later date, but must be bonded per county requirements and completed prior to expiration of bond. Each lot shall have a minimum of 50 feet of frontage.
No utilities may be placed under paved section of cul-de-sac.
(Ord. No. 2020-03, § 1(Exh. A), 8-25-2020)
1046:
Where a subdivision abuts or contains a major street, a limited access highway, or a railroad right-of-way, Meriwether County may require a street approximately parallel to and on each side of such right-of-way either as a marginal access street, or at a distance suitable for an appropriate use of the intervening land, with a non-access reservation, Due regard should be given to requirements for approach grades and future grade separation in determining distances. Such lots shall have no access to a major street (or limited access highway), but only to the access street. Acceleration and deceleration lanes may be required depending on traffic volumes and size of development, at the determination of Meriwether County.
(Ord. No. 2020-03, § 1(Exh. A), 8-25-2020)
1047:
Reserve strips which control access to streets, alleys, and public grounds shall not be permitted unless approved by Meriwether County.

1049:
(a) All new streets without curb and gutter accepted into the county road system, shall meet the following geometric requirements. All streets serving new subdivisions with lot sizes smaller than five acres are required to construct new streets using curb and gutter specifications.:
(1) Sixty-foot-wide right-of-way, legally deeded to the county, plus right-of-way for deceleration and acceleration lanes as required.
(2) Thirty-foot-wide minimum total roadbed:
a. Subdivision entry road, acceleration, and deceleration lanes as required shall have a minimum of eight-inch compacted 98 percent standard proctor graded aggregate base. Entry road must be a minimum of 20-foot wide and extend for a distance to be determined by Meriwether County, but no less than 50 feet into the subdivision.
b. Balance of subdivision streets must be 20-foot-wide road base with a minimum six-inch compacted 98 percent standard proctor graded aggregate base;
c. Minimum of two inches of 19mm asphaltic concrete binder.
d. Minimum of two inches of 9.5mm or 12.5mm of asphaltic concrete topping with bituminous tack coat
e. Asphalt construction shall conform to GDOT Section 400 Asphalt Construction Subsection 400.3.05 Paragraph E. for observed weather limitation on application.
(3) Six-foot-wide shoulders, each side, minimum, compacted soil.
(4) Six-foot-wide inside slope to ditch, each side, three to one slope or less.
(5) Two-foot-wide by two-foot deep ditches, each side.
(6) Six-foot-wide outside slope to ditch, each side, three to one slope or less.
(7) All shoulders and slopes set out in grass (Fescue, Bermuda, or approved alternative) and growth to a permanent stand must be achieved.
(8) Drainage. Drainage pipe under all driveways and street cross drains must be properly sized based on analysis of topography and hydrology of the development. Driveway pipe must be 20 feet minimum length, using county approved drainage pipe. Cross drainpipe shall be concrete and meet GDOT specifications. Headwalls meeting GDOT specifications all required at origin and terminus of culverts and crossdrains.
Street design requirements and construction are subject to inspection and approval by Meriwether County Public Works and Community Development Department. This includes, but not limited to proof rolls at various stages of construction.
(b) Before, subdivision streets are to be accepted into the public road system of Meriwether County, the following must be accomplished:
(1) The subdivision shall be platted and approved for recording, showing all street layouts, including street names.
(2) Streets will be graded, based, drained, paved, and grassed by the subdivider to Meriwether County specifications. Only one permit for a new home will be allowed until road is completed and accepted into the Meriwether County Road System.
(3) Streets will be accepted into the county road system as follows:
Streets must be constructed to all Meriwether County specifications and be approved by Meriwether County Public Works and Meriwether County Community Development Department prior to the application for acceptance into the county road system.
Request must include a warranty deed, legally conveying all rights-of-way to Meriwether County and water and sewerage utilities located within rights-of-way to Meriwether County Water and Sewerage Authority, free and clear from any liens. A maintenance bond or letter of credit is required in an amount equaling 150 percent of the roadway construction costs, made payable to Meriwether County for a three-year period following acceptance of roadway. If subdivision is less than 50 percent build out at the end of the three-year period, bond shall be extended until 50 percent build is achieved. At the end of the bonding period, Meriwether County shall inspect and require developer to make any necessary repairs to the roadway. Failure to make repairs in a timely manner will result in forfeiture of bonds. Funds from the bond forfeiture will be utilized by Meriwether County for necessary repairs to roadway.
The above refers to subdivision streets. Not included is any street that would be classified as a through street. Through streets, though built by the developer, would require different right-of-way widths and different paving specifications.
(c) Curb and gutter streets. All new streets serving subdivisions with lot sizes smaller than five acres are required to be constructed using curb and gutter specifications.
(1) Fifty feet right-of-way legally deeded to Meriwether County, plus right-of-way for deceleration and acceleration lanes as required.
(2) Subdivision entry road, acceleration, and deceleration lanes as required shall be a minimum of eight-inch compacted 98 percent standard proctor graded aggregate base. Entry road must be a minimum of 20 feet width and extend for a distance to be determined by Meriwether County, but no less than 50 feet into subdivision.
(3) Balance of subdivision streets shall be 20-foot wide road base with a minimum of six-inch compacted 98 percent standard proctor graded aggregate base.
(4) Standard six-inch by twenty-four-inch roll back curbing.
(5) Minimum of two inches 19mm Asphaltic concrete binder and minimum of two inches of 9.5mm or 12.5mm asphaltic concrete topping with bituminous tack coat meeting Meriwether County specifications.
(6) Twenty-four-foot minimum back-of-curb to back-of-curb.
(7) Asphalt construction shall conform to GDOT section 400-Asphalt Construction Standard for observed weather limitations on application.
(d) Culverts and cross drains shall meet county specifications.
(1) Concrete pipe meeting GDOT specifications and properly sized based on analysis of topography and hydrology of the development.
(2) Headwalls meeting GDOT specifications are required at origin and terminus of culverts and cross drains.
(Ord. No. 2020-03, § 1(Exh. A), 8-25-2020)

1058:
In lieu of completion of the required improvements in a subdivision, the subdivider may, if approved by Meriwether County Board of Commissioners deposit surety for the completion of such improvements and present the final plat for approval. This provision shall not apply to roads, streets, or drainage structures which are subject to other bonding requirements per this ordinance.
(Ord. No. 2020-03, § 1(Exh. A), 8-25-2020)
1059:
To ensure the construction and installation of required improvements, the subdivider upon approval by the Meriwether County Board of Commissioners shall deliver to Meriwether County, Georgia, a certified check, surety bond or other acceptable surety in such aggregate amount as is estimated by the governing authority to be the total cost of the construction and installation of all public improvements which are the responsibility of the subdivider.
(Ord. No. 2020-03, § 1(Exh. A), 8-25-2020)
1060:
Bonds or other surety posted shall run to Meriwether County, Georgia, and provide that the subdivider, his heirs or successors, and assignees and their servants will comply with all applicable terms, conditions, provisions, and requirements of these regulations and any other applicable requirements; will faithfully perform and complete the work of constructing and installing said facilities or improvements in accordance with these regulations and any other applicable requirements; and that the subdivider shall be responsible to Meriwether County, Georgia, for any unnecessary expense incurred through the failure of the subdivider, his heirs, successors and assignees, or their agents or servants, to complete the work of said construction in an acceptable manner, and from any damages growing out of negligence in performing or failing to perform said construction and installation. Before acceptance, any surety shall be approved by Meriwether County. If a bond is offered, it shall be executed by a surety or guaranty company qualified to transact business in the State of Georgia.
(Ord. No. 2020-03, § 1(Exh. A), 8-25-2020)
1061:
Bonds and/or other surety posted pursuant to these regulations shall be released or returned, as the case may be, at such time as the facilities guaranteed thereby have been installed and accepted. Acceptance shall be in writing, accurately identifying the improvements covered. Facilities shall not be accepted unless they conform to the applicable specifications and requirements.
(Ord. No. 2020-03, § 1(Exh. A), 8-25-2020)
1062:
If the construction or installation of any improvements or facilities other than streets and drainage structures for which a bond or other surety is posted is not completed within three months after substantial completion of any buildings or structures which said improvements or facilities are designed to serve, or within two years after the date of recording of the final plat, whichever is sooner, or if said construction or installation is not in accordance with the applicable specifications and requirements using the proceeds from such surety deposits to pay for such work, such work may be done under contract or by county personnel. To the extent that any portion of a cash deposit is not required or used, said excess cash shall be repaid to the person making the deposit.
(Ord. No. 2020-03, § 1(Exh. A), 8-25-2020)
